title: Claimed by 9am: 10 Study Spots Worth Showing Up Early For
description: Ten distinct Hunt Library settings for solo reading, quiet concentration, collaborative work, and reservable group sessions.

cards.entity_name: Hunt Library Group Study Room SU 347
cards.title: Put the Whole Project on the Whiteboard
cards.subtitle: A reservable third-floor room for group work
cards.notes: Reserve SU 347 in SchedulER, bring collaborators, and borrow dry-erase supplies from the Borrow Desk if your plan needs a wall-sized outline.
cards.short_summary: A bookable room suited to collaborative planning and problem-solving.
cards.evidence_claim: Hunt Library identifies SU 347 as one of five third-floor group study rooms; active affiliated students may reserve rooms through SchedulER in two-hour blocks.
cards.access_notes: For active Embry-Riddle-affiliated students. Reserve through SchedulER; reservations may total four hours daily but require separate two-hour requests.

cards.entity_name: Hunt Library Group Study Room SU 348
cards.title: Give the Study Group a Door
cards.subtitle: A reservable room across from the Borrow Desk
cards.notes: Book SU 348 before assembling your group, save the confirmation email, and keep voices measured because the library warns that rooms are not soundproof.
cards.short_summary: An enclosed collaboration space with reservations and nearby staff support.
cards.evidence_claim: The library lists SU 348 among its five large group study rooms on the third floor across from the Borrow Desk and says the rooms are not soundproof.
cards.access_notes: Restricted to active Embry-Riddle-affiliated students and reservable through SchedulER. Ask the Borrow Desk for help with reservation issues.

cards.entity_name: Hunt Library Group Study Room SU 349
cards.title: Work Through the Hard Part Together
cards.subtitle: One of four rooms accommodating groups of up to ten
cards.notes: Choose SU 349 for a larger problem set or presentation team, then divide the session into a focused agenda that fits its two-hour reservation block.
cards.short_summary: A higher-capacity room for structured team study sessions.
cards.evidence_claim: Hunt Library lists SU 349 as a reservable third-floor study room and states that four of its five large rooms accommodate as many as ten people.
cards.access_notes: Active affiliated students must log into ERNIE and use SchedulER. A confirmation email indicates whether the reservation was approved.

cards.entity_name: Hunt Library Group Study Room SU 350
cards.title: Rehearse Before the Presentation
cards.subtitle: A reservable third-floor collaboration room
cards.notes: Claim SU 350 through SchedulER for a run-through, use a small whiteboard if helpful, and leave enough time to reset the room before departure.
cards.short_summary: An enclosed setting for presentation practice and peer feedback.
cards.evidence_claim: The official policy names SU 350 as one of the library's five reservable third-floor group rooms and offers small whiteboards and markers at the Borrow Desk.
cards.access_notes: Available to active Embry-Riddle-affiliated students through SchedulER. Dry-erase markers and erasers can be checked out at the Borrow Desk.

cards.entity_name: Hunt Library Group Study Room SU 351
cards.title: Gather a Smaller Working Crew
cards.subtitle: The six-person option among Hunt Library's large rooms
cards.notes: Use SU 351 when six seats cover the team, reserve the exact time needed, and take belongings when you leave so staff do not move them to lost and found.
cards.short_summary: A six-person reservable room for compact project teams.
cards.evidence_claim: Hunt Library lists SU 351 among its five reservable rooms; its policy says one room accommodates up to six people while the other four hold up to ten.
cards.access_notes: For active affiliated students. Reserve through SchedulER in a two-hour request; unattended belongings may be removed by library or safety staff.

cards.entity_name: Hunt Library Fourth-Floor Quiet Study Space
cards.title: Move Upstairs for Quiet Work
cards.subtitle: The library's dedicated quiet-study area
cards.notes: Head to the fourth floor with reading or detail-heavy work, silence notifications, and use the area for tasks that benefit from fewer conversational distractions.
cards.short_summary: A designated quiet zone for concentrated individual work.
cards.evidence_claim: Hunt Library's official overview states that its fourth floor contains a dedicated quiet study space.
cards.access_notes: Use during posted Hunt Library hours, which vary by term and for holidays or intersessions; the library entrance is on Student Union's third floor.

cards.title: Settle Into a Carrel
cards.subtitle: Individual desks inside the Student Union library
cards.notes: Pick a carrel when you need a defined personal workspace, connect essential devices before starting, and keep the desktop reserved for the materials in use.
cards.short_summary: A bounded solo workspace for reading, writing, or review.
cards.evidence_claim: Hunt Library says its third- and fourth-floor facilities include individual study carrels among the available learning and study options.
cards.access_notes: Available within Hunt Library during its posted operating hours. Community patrons may visit and use physical materials in the facility.

cards.title: Build a Two-Person Work Session
cards.subtitle: Modern pods designed for collaborative study
cards.notes: Use a study pod for side-by-side comparison or peer review, arrive with a shared task list, and shift to a reservable room if discussion expands.
cards.short_summary: A compact collaborative setting without booking an enclosed room.
cards.evidence_claim: The library identifies collaborative pods as a study option and its official newsletter depicts a Hunt Library study pod as a modern collaborative student-study space.
cards.access_notes: Located within Hunt Library and usable during posted library hours; seating availability is not guaranteed.

cards.title: Spread Out the Shared Materials
cards.subtitle: Open tables for collaborative learning
cards.notes: Choose a collaborative table for maps, notes, or multiple laptops, agree on the next deliverable first, and keep conversation considerate of nearby readers.
cards.short_summary: Open table space for teams that need a broad shared surface.
cards.evidence_claim: Hunt Library's official description lists collaborative tables among its study and learning options and reports ample power and USB outlets for library seating.
cards.access_notes: Open seating within Hunt Library during posted hours. Power and USB outlets are available, but the university does not promise a particular seat.

cards.title: Read Away From the Group Tables
cards.subtitle: A library area arranged for leisure reading
cards.notes: Bring a long reading assignment to the leisure area, choose a comfortable seat, and use the change of posture to separate close reading from screen work.
cards.short_summary: A softer reading-oriented setting for sustained work with a text.
cards.evidence_claim: Hunt Library states that leisure reading areas are among the study and learning environments on its third and fourth floors.
cards.access_notes: Accessible within Hunt Library during current posted hours. Guests are welcome subject to library policies; specialized computer privileges are limited.
